fieldData.summary: Staff Sergeant Everette L. Williams, of Charlotte, North Carolina, was a waist gunner aboard the B-24 Liberator “Hot Rock” (serial 42-51532), the aircraft flown by the Mowat crew of the 703rd Bombardment Squadron, 445th Bombardment Group, Eighth U.S. Army Air Forces, during the Kassel Mission of 27 September 1944. The Kassel Mission was the costliest single-mission loss any U.S. heavy-bomb group suffered in the Second World War — the 445th lost twenty-five B-24 Liberators in minutes to a massed Luftwaffe attack near Eisenach. Flying as a substitute on what was to be his final mission, Staff Sergeant Williams was killed in action when “Hot Rock” went down (Missing Air Crew Report 9572); his remains were later returned to the United States and rest at the Arlington Baptist Church Cemetery in Charlotte.

fieldData.summary:
Sergeant Clare L. Wheeler, affectionately known as "Buck," was born in 1924 to Leslie and Mable Wheeler and was raised in Windsor, Wisconsin. He graduated from DeForest Area High School and later enlisted in the U.S. Army Air Corps during World War II. Serving as a tail gunner in the 703rd Bomb Squadron of the 445th Bomb Group, Sgt. Wheeler participated in several critical missions.

On September 27, 1944, Sgt. Wheeler was tragically killed in action during the Kassel Mission.

His remains were returned to his family for reburial several years later. Sgt. Wheeler is interred at the Windsor Congregational Cemetery in Windsor, Wisconsin.

For more detailed information about Sgt. Wheeler's life and service, you may visit the DeForest Area Historical Society's page dedicated to him.
fieldData.name: Clare L. Wheeler

A FULL LIFE

Carrow, Raphael Edwin

February 24, 2009, of Torrance, CA, age 90, formerly of New York and Miami. Born in Brooklyn, NY to Samuel and Ethel Cohen.

First Lieutenant US Army Air Force 445th Bomb Group in WWII. Pilot of a B-24 bomber shot down in the Kassel Mission over Germany and taken prisoner in 1944. Awarded the Purple Heart and Air Medal among others. Graduate of the Univ. of Wisconsin, Madison 1940. His career covered real estate, investments and the US Bureau of Labor Statistics. Beloved husband of the late Carmen (nee Amaro), he is survived by brother Milton (Barbara); children with former late wife Beverly: Grant (Deborah), Stephanie, Breck (Paula); grandchildren Lissette Serota (Todd), Sussette Haubert, Daniel Carrow, Stephen Carrow; great granddaughters Kayla Haubert, Raina Serota, Maya Serota and many nieces and nephews. Predeceased by sister Sylvia Cabiac. A memorial service will be held at a later date. Donations in his memory may be made to the Kassel Mission Historical Society (KMHS), P.O. Box 215133, Auburn Hills, MI 48321 (kasselmission.com) or The Parkinson's Institute (thepi.org).

He will be profoundly missed and we will keep the memories of him alive.

Published in the Los Angeles Times from Mar. 1 to Mar. 30, 2009

2nd Lieutenant George R. Austin served as a navigator in the U.S. Army Air Forces during World War II. His aircraft, a B-24 Liberator nicknamed "Patches" (serial number 42-110022), was shot down during this Kassel Mission. While some crew members survived the initial bailout, they were subsequently captured and killed, with Lt. Austin being one of them.

For additional information about Lt. Austin's service and the circumstances of his death, you can visit his profile on the American Air Museum's website.

From Mike Simpson, 445th Bomb Group Historian:

According to the crew loading lists, Palmer Bruland flew 19 missions as co-pilot for Harold Wolgang in the 701st Bomb Squadron. Palmer took on a new crew as 1st Pilot starting with 445th mission #160 on 09 Sept 44.

Wolgang crew, stateside training photo, above. Palmer Bruland standing 2nd from right. Harold Wolgang went on to fly another 10 missions after Bruland left to begin flying as a 1st Pilot.

Bruland’s missions as 1st Pilot were:

  • 09 Sep 44 – Mainz, Germany; Railroad marshalling yard
  • 10 Sep 44 – Ulm, Germany; Ordnance depot
  • 11 Sep 44 – Misburg, Germany; Oil refinery
  • 12 Sep 44 – Misburg, Germany; Oil refinery
  • 13 Sep 44 – Ulm, Germany; Ulm motor transport works
  • 22 Sep 44 – Kassel, Germany; Kassel locomotive works
  • 25 Sep 44 – Koblenz, Germany; Mosel railroad marshalling yard
  • 26 Sep 44 – Hamm, Germany; Railroad marshalling yard
  • 27 Sep 44 – Kassel, Germany; Henschel armored vehicle assembly plant

SHORT ACCOUNT

Written to German historian, Walter Hassenpflug, in 1987

SHOT DOWN

LIBERATED AND REPATRIATED

HONORABLY DISCHARGED

After the war, Palmer Bruland obtained his civilian's private and commercial pilot's licenses.

fieldData.summary:
First Lieutenant Donald Eugene Brent was born on December 22, 1916, in Weiser, Idaho, to George and Jessie Brent. He later moved to Oregon, where he enlisted in the U.S. Army Air Forces during World War II. As a B-24 Liberator pilot assigned to the 702nd Bombardment Squadron of the 445th Bomb Group, Lt. Brent flew numerous missions over Europe.

Lt. Brent's aircraft, nicknamed "Eileen," was severely damaged by enemy fighters on September 27, 1944. He ordered his crew to bail out; however, his parachute failed to deploy properly, and he was killed in action. Initially reported as missing, his status was later confirmed as killed in action.

Lt. Brent was posthumously awarded the Distinguished Flying Cross, the Air Medal with three Oak Leaf Clusters, and the Purple Heart. He is buried at the Ardennes American Cemetery and Memorial in Neuville-en-Condroz, Belgium.
fieldData.name: Donald E. Brent

fieldData.summary: Second Lieutenant Hektor V. Scala was the bombardier aboard the B-24 Liberator “King Kong” (serial 42-50383), the aircraft flown by the Baynham crew of the 702nd Bombardment Squadron, 445th Bombardment Group, Eighth U.S. Army Air Forces, during the Kassel Mission of 27 September 1944. The Kassel Mission was the costliest single-mission loss any U.S. heavy-bomb group suffered in the Second World War — the 445th lost twenty-five B-24 Liberators in minutes to a massed Luftwaffe attack near Eisenach. After parachuting safely to the ground at Nentershausen, Lieutenant Scala surrendered unarmed but was beaten and shot to death — a war crime later documented in the United Nations War Crimes Commission files as Case No. 253.
